# RV power station and solar combo picks

For an RV, the deciding factor is the roof air conditioner. A 13,500 BTU unit draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). If you want to run the AC, you need roughly 3,000W or more of output. If you only run a fridge, lights, a laptop and Starlink, a ~1,000-2,000Wh unit is enough.

## Top picks

**1. Best value for big output: ALLPOWERS R4000**
- It has 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V (6,000W peak), an RV outlet, and LiFePO4 cells rated for 3,500+ cycles.
- Solar input is up to 2,000W over three inputs of 650W each, so you need panels on all three to hit that.
- The store price is $1,499. With code EXTRA12 (12% off orders over $1,200, expires 11/15), Dealectric reports $1,319.12. The store accepts one code per order.
- It has a 5-year warranty. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's more of an install-in-place unit than a carry-around one.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you). Details are on the [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh).

**2. Best for full-time boondocking: EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3**
- It has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous, 8,000W surge, expansion past 12kWh, and about 0 to 80% in 50 minutes from a wall outlet ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- It's the most expensive option, and it's heavy enough to be a two-person lift.

**3. Simplest for running the AC: Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro**
- It has 3,024Wh, 3,000W, 6,000W surge, and can start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).

**4. Mid-range with a 30A RV port: BLUETTI AC200L**
- It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W, up to 1,200W solar input, and weighs about 62 lb ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)). It suits fridge, electronics and light loads better than AC.

**Weekend or light use:** The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus (1,024Wh, up to 1,000W solar, about 28 lb) and the Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (1,070Wh, 400W solar cap, about 24 lb) both fit here ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).

## Solar panel pairing
- Match your array to the station's solar input limit. A bigger array than the limit is wasted, and an undersized one charges slowly ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).
- A 300-400W folding array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- For a Jackery 1000 v2, two 200W SolarSaga panels use its full 400W input ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- For a roof-mounted or larger setup, the R4000 would need panels on three inputs, each up to 650W.
- Renogy's 200W foldable solar suitcase is mentioned as a pairing in [NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife).

## Caveats
- The search results didn't include direct purchase links for the EcoFlow, Jackery, Bluetti or panel products, so I can't give you verified buy links for them. Check current price and specs on each manufacturer's or Amazon's page before ordering.
- Most of these sources earn affiliate commissions, and the EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, Canada. Its safety rules (like electrician requirements) may differ from your local ones. Have a licensed electrician do any hardwired connection to your RV.
- Prices and specs differ between sources, so confirm them before buying.

If you tell me your RV type, whether you want to run the AC off-grid, and your budget, I can narrow this to one station and a specific panel setup.
